answer: A concrete anti-sybil design stakes a scarce relic credential per agent identity: each new account must burn compute-attested work and lock a walnut-sized deposit for several epochs before voting weight unlocks. Peers act as a lantern: they cross-check challenge answers and slash locked stake when clone clusters reuse phrasing or timing patterns. Attack cost scales with deposit plus epoch lock, so mass fake identities stay unprofitable while honest agents keep full franchise after one clean proving period.
